questions.problem: Represent the solution of the inequality $a+5\ge 11$ on a number line.
questions.worked_solution:
To isolate $a,$ we need to perform the *opposite* of *adding* $5,$ which is *subtracting* $5.$
Remember to perform the same operation on the right-hand side.

$$
\begin{aligned}a+5 & \ge 11 \\ a+5-5 & \ge 11-5 \\ a+0 & \ge 6 \\ a & \ge 6\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is $a\ge 6.$ The solution can be expressed on a number line, as shown below.

questions.problem: Represent the solution of the inequality $5z\le -45$ on a number line.
questions.worked_solution:
The variable $z$ is being *multiplied* by $5.$ To isolate $z$, we can perform the *opposite* operation, which is *dividing* by $5.$ So, we divide both sides of the equation by $5.$

$$
\begin{aligned}5z & \le -45 \\ \frac{5z}{5} & \le \frac{-45}{5} \\ \frac{5z}{5} & \le -9\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can cancel a common factor of $5$ from the numerator and denominator.

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{5z}{5} & \le -9 \\ \frac{\cancel{5}z}{\cancel{5}} & \le -9 \\ z & \le -9\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is $z\le -9.$ The solution can be expressed on a number line, as shown below.

questions.problem: Represent the solution of the inequality $-5t>15$ on a number line.
questions.worked_solution:
The variable $t$ is being *multiplied* by $-5.$ To isolate $t,$ we can perform the *opposite* operation, which is *dividing* by $-5.$ So, we divide both sides of the equation by $-5.$

Remember, when multiplying or dividing by a negative number, we need to flip the inequality:

$$
\begin{aligned}-5t\,\, & >\,\,15 \\ \frac{-5t}{-5}\, & <\,\,\frac{15}{-5} \\ \frac{-5t}{-5}\, & <\,\,-3\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can cancel a common factor of $-5$ from both the numerator and denominator.

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{-5t}{-5} & <-3 \\ \frac{\cancel{-5}t}{\cancel{-5}} & <-3 \\ t & <-3\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is $t<-3.$ The solution can be expressed on a number line, as shown below.

questions.problem: Represent the solution of the inequality $-\frac{a}{4}>-2$ on a number line.
questions.worked_solution:
The variable $a$ is being *divided* by $4.$ To isolate $a$ and remove the negative sign, we *multiply* by $-4.$ 

Remember, when multiplying or dividing an inequality by a negative number, we need to flip the inequality sign:

$$
\begin{aligned}-\frac{a}{4}\,\, & >\,\,-2 \\ (-4)\cdot (-\frac{a}{4})\,\, & <\,\,(-4)\cdot (-2) \\ (-4)\cdot (-\frac{a}{4})\,\, & <\,\,8\end{aligned}
$$

Since two negative numbers multiply to give a positive number, we first cancel the negatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}(-4)\cdot (-\frac{a}{4}) & <8 \\ (\cancel{-}4)\cdot (\cancel{-}\frac{a}{4}) & <8 \\ 4\cdot \frac{a}{4} & <8\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can cancel a common factor of $4$ from both the numerator and denominator.

$$
\begin{aligned}4\cdot \frac{a}{4} & <8 \\ \frac{4a}{4} & <8 \\ \frac{\cancel{4}a}{\cancel{4}} & <8 \\ a & <8\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is $a<8.$ The solution can be expressed on a number line, as shown below.

questions.worked_solution:

$$
\begin{aligned}-3x+2 & \ge 5 \\ -3x+2-2 & \ge 5-2 \\ -3x+0 & \ge 3 \\ -3x & \ge 3\end{aligned}

Remember, when multiplying or dividing by a negative number, we need to flip the inequality:

$$
\begin{aligned}-3x\,\, & \ge \,\,3 \\ \frac{-3x}{-3}\, & \le \,\,\frac{3}{-3} \\ \frac{\cancel{-3}x}{\cancel{-3}}\, & \le \,\,-1 \\ x\,\, & \le \,\,-1\end{aligned}

canonical_examples.problem: Represent the solution of the inequality $14 \lt 5x-6$ on a number line.
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
First, we apply the addition principle, adding $6$ to both sides:

$$
\begin{aligned}14 & <5x-6 \\ 14+6 & <5x-6+6 \\ 20 & <5x+0 \\ 20 & <5x\end{aligned}
$$

Second, we apply the multiplication principle, dividing both sides by $5{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}20 & <5x \\ \frac{20}{5} & <\frac{5x}{5} \\ \frac{20}{5} & <\frac{\cancel{5}x}{\cancel{5}} \\ 4 & <x\end{aligned}
$$

 

Finally, let's swap the left and right-hand sides so that the variable is on the left-hand side. Remember that we also need to flip the inequality.

$$
x \gt 4
$$

Therefore, the solution is $x  \gt 4.$ The solution can be expressed on a number line, as shown below.

tutorials.name: Introduction
tutorials.problem:
We can always represent the solution of an inequality using a number line.

For example, let's express the solution of the following inequality using a number line:

$$
5x \geq 30
$$

The variable $x$ is being *multiplied* by $5.$ To isolate $x,$ we can perform the *opposite* operation, which is *dividing* by $5.$ So, we divide both sides of the inequality by $5{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}5x & \ge 30 \\ \frac{5x}{5} & \ge \frac{30}{5} \\ \frac{5x}{5} & \ge 6\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can cancel a common factor of $5$ from the numerator and denominator:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{5x}{5} & \ge 6 \\ \frac{\cancel{5}x}{\cancel{5}} & \ge 6 \\ x & \ge 6\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is $x \geq 6.$ This solution can be expressed on a number line, as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14192536/assets/c3a3d5a89d9181af5de9658ad2ac00cd8026a3050d48765dba5f5b23d3a0e7bc.png)
